author: Peninsula Quiet Guide
title: Free Summer 2026 Concerts and Movies for Families in Menlo Park, Palo Alto, and Redwood City
text:
16 hours ago Summer 2026 on the mid-Peninsula is the cheapest, easiest weeknight out a parent can build. Three cities — Menlo Park, Palo Alto, and Redwood City — are running overlapping free outdoor concert, movie, and plaza series from early June through late August. All of them are stroller-friendly. None of them charge a dime. Most of them put a playground or a concession tent within sight of the lawn.
This is the planning version of the list. Pick three or four nights across the summer. Block them on the family calendar. Done.
The most locked-in calendar of the three cities is Menlo Park's Summer Concert Series .
Karl E. Clark Park — photo 3 — Mickelin Burnes-Browne — source Karl E. Clark Park — photo 2 — Sumudu Leelananda — source Karl E. Clark Park — photo 1 — Paul-Elie Nauleau — source The City of Menlo Park has published the full 2026 lineup: eight free concerts, all starting at 6 p.m., split between Fremont Park and Karl E. Clark Park. The city's own copy says it plainly — "Grab your lawn chairs and blankets, and pack all your favorite picnic essentials."
The Wednesday-night Fremont Park lineup runs July 8 (Boys of Summer, Eagles tribute), July 15 (Fog City Swampers, classic rock and CCR), July 22 (Fast Times, 80s dance hits), July 29 (Smokin' Slice of Mojo, soul and R&B), August 5 (Given to Fly, cosmic pop/rock/soul), and August 12 (The Sun Kings, Beatles tribute) . The Beatles tribute closes the series. That one is a multi-generational easy win — parents recognize every song, an eight-year-old picks up the choruses by the third number.
Fremont Park is at 915 Santa Cruz Ave , walking distance from the entire downtown Menlo Park dining strip.
Veterans gathered at Fremont Park, Menlo Park, CA for WWI centennial commemoration (2018) — InMenlo — source Busta Groove summer concert at Fremont Park, Menlo Park, CA (July 2024) — InMenlo — source Fremont Park shaded grass area and tall heritage tree, Menlo Park, CA — City of Menlo Park — source The right move: feed the family first on Santa Cruz Ave, then walk over with chairs and a blanket. Arrive before 5:45 p.m. for a flat spot near a tree. The series is sponsored by The Almanac and West Bay Sanitary District. Series info line: 650-330-2200.
The two Karl E. Clark Park dates are the differentiated picks. Friday, July 31 brings Patrón Latin Rhythms (Latin fusion). Friday, August 7 brings Curley Taylor & Zydeco Trouble. Both start at 6 p.m. Smaller crowd than Fremont Park, neighborhood-park feel, kids actually dance. If the eight-year-old is itching to move, the zydeco night is the one.
Twenty miles up El Camino, Redwood City's Music on the Square is hitting its 20th anniversary in 2026. Fourteen free Friday-night concerts at Courthouse Square (2200 Broadway) , 6–8 p.m., with the Santana tribute Carnaval confirmed as the season opener and pop/soul band Pride & Joy as the closer.
Courthouse Square — photo 3 — George Shih — source Courthouse Square — photo 2 — Mihir Shah — source Courthouse Square — photo 1 — Odin — source The City's official page calls it "20 years of live music and community celebration." Specific Friday-by-Friday dates have not been posted on the city site as of this writing — check redwoodcity.org/musiconthesquare before locking a date.
The Square is surrounded by 25-plus downtown restaurants. Grab takeout from any of them and walk it back to the lawn. Limited seating provided on-site; bring chairs anyway. Restrooms are inside the adjacent county buildings during daytime hours; expect lines once the crowd settles.
The same Courthouse Square hosts Movies on the Square on Thursdays. The 2026 series runs 12 weeks starting Thursday, June 4 , and stretches through late August. It is a true outdoor double feature: a kids' film around 6 p.m., followed by the main feature around 8:30 p.m. (BraveMaker Independent shorts run around 8 p.m. on alternating weeks). The setup is a "giant LED screen, complete with surround sound." A FIFA World Cup live viewing party slots in once midseason.
This is the right pick for households with two kids on different schedules. The eight-year-old gets the early film and goes home. The eleven-year-old can stay for the feature. Limited tables and chairs on-site — bring blankets. Source: redwoodcity.org/residents/redwood-city-events/movies. Series info line: 650-780-7311.
The quieter Redwood City option is Music in the Park at Stafford Park (King Street and Hopkins Avenue) — Wednesday evenings, 6–8 p.m., shifting to 5:30–7:30 p.m. for the late-August dates.
Stafford Park — photo 3 — Scott Smith — source Stafford Park — photo 2 — Puneet Chugh — source Stafford Park — photo 1 — Benjamin H — source Redwood City Parks confirmed a 10-week run for 2026. The 2026 lineup opens with Brazilian-jazz vocalist Masha Campagne. Funk, soul, Latin rock, bluegrass, and "just-for-kids" shows fill in the rest. Specific weekly dates and the full performer list were not yet posted at time of writing — confirm at redwoodcity.org/musicinthepark.
Stafford Park has the best logistics in the entire summer slate for a working-parent weeknight. There is an on-site concession tent — burgers, hot dogs, chips, drinks. No takeout run required. The playground is right next to the lawn, so kids can rotate between the music and the slide. Smaller, quieter, more local-family than the downtown Music on the Square crowd.
For one Saturday on the calendar, the City of Redwood City has confirmed a Classical on the Square evening with the Redwood Symphony at Courthouse Square, 7 p.m. The exact 2026 date was still listed as "COMING SOON" on the official Classical on the Square page at time of writing. Historically the series has been a one-off in late June. If the kid is starting to ask about real instruments, this is the gateway show — outdoor, casual, no ticket, no dress code, full orchestra.
In Palo Alto, the City's free Twilight Concert Series returns for 2026 with three planned shows across Rinconada Park (777 Embarcadero Road) , Mitchell Park (600 East Meadow Drive) , and California Avenue .
Rinconada Cultural Park — photo 3 — Shahab Mousavi — source Rinconada Cultural Park — photo 2 — Carlos Reyes — source Rinconada Cultural Park — photo 1 — Diana Alvarez Kaba — source Concerts begin at 6:30 p.m., run about 90 minutes — the right pre-bedtime length — and feature food trucks on-site. The 2026 schedule lives at paloalto.gov/Events-Directory/Community-Services/Twilight-Concert-Series-2026; specific dates and acts had not been publicly posted at time of writing.
The Rinconada Park show is the standout. The lawn sits next to the Magical Bridge Playground and the Junior Museum & Zoo . Play first, eat from a food truck, then settle on the grass for the band. Elementary-aged kids are in their element. If a guide had to pick one Palo Alto date for a family with a third-grader and a sixth-grader, this is it.
The other Palo Alto pick is the Family Movie Night Series at Mitchell Park's southeast athletic field . The City of Palo Alto Community Services has confirmed the 5th annual edition for summer 2026. Seating opens around 7 p.m. The film starts at sundown. Recent-release animated and family titles have headlined past lineups — Despicable Me 4, Moana 2, Mufasa, The Wild Robot. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, snacks. Series info line: 650-329-2241. Specific 2026 titles and dates had not been posted at time of writing.
One emerging option to flag: Palo Alto Online previewed a new evening concert series at EPACenter in East Palo Alto for summer 2026. A few minutes from both Menlo Park and Palo Alto. Worth watching the announcement, especially if the regular slate fills up.
How to actually plan this: do not try to hit everything. Pick three nights for the summer. One Menlo Park concert on a Wednesday — the August 12 Beatles tribute is the safest pick. One Redwood City night that doubles as dinner downtown — either a Friday Music on the Square or a Thursday Movies on the Square depending on whether the kids want music or a film. One Palo Alto night that uses the playground angle — Rinconada Park if the Twilight schedule lines up, Mitchell Park's movie night if it doesn't.
Add Stafford Park's Music in the Park as the backup plan for any week the calendar collapses. The on-site burgers and the adjacent playground mean nobody has to cook, change clothes, or pre-plan dinner.
Save this list. Bookmark four URLs — the Menlo Park concert series page, redwoodcity.org/musiconthesquare, redwoodcity.org/musicinthepark, and paloalto.gov's Twilight Concert and Family Movie Night pages. Check them once in late May for the dates that are still pending. Then put the three picks on the family calendar before June 1, before everything else fills the summer.
Free, walkable, weeknight-length, kid-tolerant. That is the entire pitch.
summary: Fourteen free Friday-night concerts at Courthouse Square (2200 Broadway) , 6–8 p.m., with the Santana tribute Carnaval confirmed as the season opener and pop/soul band Pride & Joy as the closer. Restrooms are inside the adjacent county buildings during daytime hours; expect lines once the crowd settles. If the kid is starting to ask about real instruments, this is the gateway show — outdoor, casual, no ticket, no dress code, full orchestra. The other Palo Alto pick is the Family Movie Night Series at Mitchell Park's southeast athletic field .
